title: One-direction propagation and the remaining characteristic strata
source_hypothesis: Scalar properly supported classical order-one P with principal symbol tau+i f and f<=0 near a compact real tau ray; Pu microlocally H(s), incoming u microlocally H(s). The imaginary symbol may depend on all momenta. Characteristic classification is on the regular locus under condition P.
reviewed_arguments: The characteristic register uses whole regular rank-one curves, not pointwise Hessian tests. All extensions are invariant and conic, the disjoint decomposition is explicit, and the residual class has a complete third-order Taylor representation on ordinary compact tubes including radial arcs.

The printed source sign was visually verified: forward propagation for D=-i partial uses f<=0 in tau+i f. The earlier private OCR interpretation is superseded by an exact-page reading correction; no delivered theorem used its reversed sign.

The full scalar order-one statement allows all-real Sobolev orders and arbitrary distributions. Compact conic localization and a global nonpositive symbol extension retain every lower-order and smoothing error; the one-dimensional elliptic analogue is included.

The symmetric imaginary part has a sharp upper form bound independent of the weight and regularizer. Exact common cutoff factors make the outgoing quadratic term nonnegative before its minus sign is used.
The purely imaginary principal symbol of the imaginary-part commutator cancels upon symmetrizing. Full uniform remainders are of order 2s-1 and are controlled at the exact weak order s-1/2.
The weighted identity is justified on the actual Sobolev domains. Its leading absorption constant is independent of the weight, which is fixed before all remaining estimates.

An explicit first-order composition expansion moves the regularizer to the left. The complete order-s-2 remainder and finite localized forcing tests bound every regularized source and incoming term uniformly.

Fourier dominated convergence identifies the distributional limit; the proved Hilbert weak subsequence argument puts it in L2. A finite half-order bootstrap treats every distribution. An infinite nested family with positive limiting width gives actual smoothness on one fixed cone.

Three solved exercises check the scalar energy sign, construct an exact flat-damping solution with a singular incoming side and smooth outgoing side, and distinguish an isolated zero Hessian from the residual characteristic set.

Twenty-four exact finite identities passed. The full desktop reader, two mobile samples and original figure were inspected; the figure axes and crossing Hessian label were corrected. Every mobile display and figure extent was measured.

Continue with shrinking real cutoffs, complex-cutoff energy, intrinsic directed propagation and prescribed concave regularity. These readings keep the indefinite affine scope and the semidefinite rank obstruction.
